newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev eases on value date, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev eases on value date, seen stable.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev traded between 1,485-1,500 per dollar at the opening, down from 1,475-1,485 at the close of the interbank market on Wednesday due to the longer value date of spot deals, dealers said.
"The lev eased by some 10 to 15 (levs per dollar) from yesterday because of the longer value date of spot deals, which falls on May 2," a commercial bank dealer said.
Markets will be closed in Bulgaria from Monday through Thursday for Eastern Orthodox Easter.

Some traders tested lower levels for the lev at 1,515-1,520 at the very opening but there was no foreign currency demand at those levels as the market expected the lev to trade stable or strengthen further, dealers said.
Ample dollar supply from local and foreign investors eyeing high yield local debt has supported the lev stable around 1,500 since early March.

The large spread between interest rates on dollar- and lev-denominated investments leaves room for the local currency to dip by four levs against the dollar daily under current exchange rate and main interest rate, dealers said.
The Bulgarian National Bank main interest rate is now set at 8.03 percent monthly or 96.36 percent annually. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
